summary: Part 4 of Parkevtate Vosianc CFA's Nike deep dive (published 2026-09-21) argues Nike's latest quarter was worse than the headline numbers suggested. Management disclosed that sales started strongly in May (especially North America) but decelerated through the quarter — the worst pattern an investor can see, since it signals declining momentum likely to bleed into the next quarter. He ties the slowdown to re-escalating Middle East conflict (after a temporary US/Israel/Iran pause) driving oil prices higher and squeezing discretionary spending, with Nike squarely at the epicenter. He praises management's prudent response — cutting inventory, focusing on full-price sell-through — while stressing Nike can do nothing about the macro backdrop. A Supreme Court ruling refunding ~$986 million in previously paid (deemed illegal) tariffs is framed as mere relief, not a fix: tariffs remain a volatile, unpredictable headwind as the administration uses trade barriers as pressure, which he argues actually deters US manufacturing investment. With nearly all manufacturing overseas, Nike has no realistic US-reshoring option. Bottom line: 3–6 more months of difficulty ahead. Call: NKE UNCERTAIN.
